decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3: “pasting an address creates a readable bookmark automatically”; client entry 4: “that's exactly the right direction.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level save-and-readable-display decision during requirements confirmation.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3 only says labels organize links; client entry 4 adds: “I want to be able to click a label and see only the links with that label.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing tag-filter behavior during requirements confirmation.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3 presents labels and search separately; client entry 4 adds: “I want search and labels to work together.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing combined narrowing behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3 does not specify opening saved targets; client entry 4 adds: “tapping it should take me straight to the actual page.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing navigation requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 asks whether the saved item has the expected content; client entry 8 reports title, description, and source, but neither entry establishes whether favicon and preview image are collected or whether a favicon is exposed in the list.
decisions.note: The recorded save presentation is insufficient to determine compliance with the remaining metadata and favicon requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 presents a “single paste-and-save area”; client entry 8 describes pasting the URL and immediately selecting Save, with title and description filled only on the resulting card, and approves the flow.
decisions.note: The presented save flow provides no opportunity to edit collected title or description before saving; the client does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 assumes new links begin as “To read”; client entry 8 explicitly agrees.
decisions.note: Conforming unread/read-later initialization decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, maker entry 9 says selecting the card opens the original MDN page; client entry 10 confirms that the whole card opened the actual page.
decisions.note: Conforming original-URL navigation decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, maker entry 9 has the client save the same address again without explaining duplicate handling; client entry 10 says it “shouldn't quietly make a second copy” and should recognize the existing link and take her to it for updating.
decisions.note: The client corrects the initially opaque duplicate-save behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, maker entry 11 presents a duplicate notice, one retained copy, and attention drawn to the existing card; client entry 12 says she will later want to “open it up and change things on it,” but accepts that as “a separate flow” and says the current duplicate handling is right.
decisions.note: The revised flow identifies and highlights the existing item but does not yet guide directly into editing; the client states that difference and accepts it for this stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, maker entry 13 offers three ways to add `reference`; client entry 14 selects the inline input and confirms that the label chip appears.
decisions.note: All offered interaction variants permit tag assignment; the selected layout preference is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, maker entry 13 presents label entry without reuse suggestions; client entry 14 requests suggestions for previously used labels while typing.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing existing-tag autocomplete requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, maker entry 15 presents collection-wide, capitalization-insensitive prefix suggestions; client entry 16 confirms that choosing `reference` reuses its established spelling.
decisions.note: Conforming tag-autocomplete revision.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, maker entry 17 presents filtering by either a bookmark chip or the label row; client entry 18 confirms only the two `javascript` bookmarks remain.
decisions.note: Conforming specific-tag filter decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, maker entry 19 keeps the selected `javascript` label active while `guides` narrows the results; client entry 20 confirms each condition tightens the result.
decisions.note: Conforming combination of tag filtering and text search.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, maker entry 19 explicitly scopes search to “titles, descriptions, and source names”; client entry 20 approves those fields and does not request searching the complete saved URL.
decisions.note: A source/hostname search is not equivalent to full-text search over the complete URL, and the difference is not surfaced.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, maker entry 19 omits notes from the searchable fields; client entry 20 states that search should eventually look inside notes but says, “Not asking you to build it this second.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies the missing note-search expectation while accepting its absence in this prototype stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, maker entry 19 says search ignores capitalization; client entry 20 says this is important and correct.
decisions.note: Conforming case-insensitive search decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, maker entry 21 offers controls for changing To read to Done; client entry 22 selects the two-way toggle and emphasizes that Done can be moved back to To read.
decisions.note: Conforming reversible read/unread status decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, maker entry 23 presents separate To read and Done views with immediate movement; client entry 24 selects top tabs and confirms the completed bookmark disappears from To read and appears in Done.
decisions.note: Conforming separate-unread-view and mark-read behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, maker entry 25 presents editing title, note, and labels together; client entry 26 confirms all three changes were retained.
decisions.note: Conforming presented portions of bookmark editing and tag assignment.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, maker entry 25's edit panel includes title, note, and labels; client entry 26 says description editing is missing and asks for it in the same panel.
decisions.note: The client requests the missing post-save description editor.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, maker entry 25's edit panel omits the address; client entry 26 says she could not fix the web address and asks for it in the panel.
decisions.note: The client separately requests the missing URL editor.

decisions.evidence: Round 14, maker entry 27 presents description and URL editing while preserving other details; client entry 28 confirms both changes and preservation.
decisions.note: Conforming revised post-save edit behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 14, maker entry 27 asks whether the full address should remain visible during normal use; client entry 28 selects a clean card with only the short source and keeps the full URL in editing.
decisions.note: Faced with a production-display choice, the client selects the reference-conforming readability-first alternative.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 13–14, maker entries 25 and 27 present writing and displaying a plain note, and client entries 26 and 28 approve it; the record never establishes Markdown input or rendered Markdown behavior.
decisions.note: The general note behavior is demonstrated, but compliance with the Markdown-specific portion cannot be determined.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 presents capitalization-insensitive note search that remains combinable with labels; client entry 30 confirms `closures` matches only the note-bearing bookmark.
decisions.note: Conforming revision adding note text to full-text search.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 asks whether note search completes search; client entry 30 says she also wants to type `#reference` in the search box.
decisions.note: The client requests the missing inline tag-search syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 asks whether search is complete; client entry 30 requests AND/OR/NOT combinations and parenthesized grouping.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing Boolean-search grammar.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 asks whether search is complete; client entry 30 requests quoted exact phrases.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing exact-phrase requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 16, maker entry 31 presents `closures #reference`, case-insensitive tag names, and AND semantics for multiple tags; client entry 32 confirms all behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming inline tag-search decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 presents `rome AND (#article OR #book) AND NOT ancient`; client entry 34 confirms grouping, OR, AND, and immediate NOT exclusion.
decisions.note: Conforming demonstrated Boolean and parenthesized-search behavior.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 17–18, maker entries 33 and 35 demonstrate operators and quoted phrases, but neither presentation nor response tests or specifies quoting an operator such as `"AND"` to search for it literally.
decisions.note: The record cannot establish compliance or divergence for the required literal-operator rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 presents adjacent, same-order, capitalization-insensitive matching for `"a weekend"`; client entry 36 confirms the noncontiguous result is excluded.
decisions.note: Conforming exact-phrase search decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 19, maker entry 37 blocks `not a web address`, preserves the input, and shows a complete-address example; client entry 38 confirms no invalid bookmark is created.
decisions.note: Conforming enforcement of the required-URL constraint.

decisions.evidence: Round 20, maker entry 39 saves a valid URL even when metadata loading fails, uses a temporary source title, and points to editing; client entry 40 approves preserving the link and fixing details later.
decisions.note: Conforming save-and-later-edit recovery decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 23, maker entry 45 presents duplicate recognition after removing known tracking parameters and a fragment; client entry 46 confirms one copy remains and the existing bookmark is indicated.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate convergence with a reasonable normalization extension.

decisions.evidence: Round 24, maker entry 47 reuses established lowercase `reference` even when `REFERENCE` is directly submitted; client entry 48 confirms no capitalization variant is created.
decisions.note: Conforming tag-uniqueness behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 26, maker entry 51 offers preservation without active monitoring; client entry 52 accepts no monitoring but adds that initial save should keep a copy of the page as it existed then.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing snapshot-preservation requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 27, maker entry 53 presents automatic capture of a readable preserved copy and access inside Link Home; client entry 54 confirms the copy is captured at save time and opens as the preserved version.
decisions.note: Conforming core snapshot decision.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 27–28, maker entries 53 and 55 refer generically to a “readable page copy”; client entries 54 and 56 approve that behavior, but the record never identifies single-file HTML storage or the required PDF-download exception.
decisions.note: The snapshot presentation does not provide enough evidence to determine the format and PDF-specific rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 29, maker entry 57 offers treatments for long descriptions and notes; client entry 58 selects compact cards with in-place Show more/Show less and full content remaining accessible.
decisions.note: Conforming readability-first display with access to complete note and description content.

decisions.evidence: Round 30, maker entry 59 presents an empty Done tab with a route back to To read; client entry 60 confirms the separate To read collection remains available and unchanged.
decisions.note: Conforming separate status-view behavior in the empty-state case.

decisions.evidence: Round 31, maker entry 61 presents all-or-nothing validation for an edit containing an invalid URL; client entry 62 confirms pending edits remain and only apply together after correction.
decisions.note: Conforming robust bookmark-edit behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 33, maker entry 65 presents the implemented first-cycle app; client entry 66 says she inspected it and explicitly identifies paste-and-save, label syntax and filters, phrase/Boolean search, status tabs, complete edit fields, duplicates, and preserved copies as matching the approved flows.
decisions.note: Implementation-review decision for the reference-conforming behaviors the client directly identifies; it does not establish unmentioned reference features.
